title: O Come and Dwell in Me
description: O Come and Dwell in Me in Tonic Solfa to BOYLSTON, doh is C: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 3 verses and a piano.
about: Charles Wesley wrote these words. They were printed in the supplement of the 1866 edition of A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion, compiled by Samuel Longfellow and Samuel Johnson (Boston, 1866), as hymn 517, “Aspiration”.
The book printed the words without tunes, marked Short Metre (6.6.8.6), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to BOYLSTON; any other Short Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: O come and dwell in me, Spirit of po-wer with-in! And bring Thy glo-rious lib-er-ty From sor-row, fear and sin.

lines: O come and dwell in me,
When old things shall be done away,

source: A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion (1848)
licence: Public domain: Charles Wesley died in 1788.
credits: Words by Charles Wesley (1707–1788), public domain, as printed in A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion (1866); set to BOYLSTON by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
